title: Dewey on the web and silos in 1934
summary: All communication is like art. It may fairly be said, therefore, that any social arrangement that remains vitally social, or vitally shared, is educative to those who participate in it. Only when it becomes cast in a mold and runs in a routine way does it lose its educative power. It's like Dewey knew what would happen if we didn't drive people onto the web
author: Greg McVerry
body_html:
All communication is like art. It may fairly be said, therefore, that any social arrangement that remains vitally social, or vitally shared, is educative to those who participate in it. Only when it becomes cast in a mold and runs in a routine way does it lose its educative power.

It's like Dewey knew what would happen if we didn't drive people onto the web
